messages.content: That's good to know. I'll go check the soil then. I was also wondering, do you think I should move any of them out of the direct sun? Some of the leaves are starting to look a little droopy.

Moving them out of the direct sun sounds like a very good idea right now, especially if they are starting to look droopy. If you're worried about the heat, putting them in a spot that gets filtered or dappled light should help significantly.
I'll try that. I'm also worried about the uneven heat in the house—some rooms are sweltering and others are still cool. Do you think I should rotate them more often?

That's a smart thought. If the heat is uneven, it can be stressful for the plants. While they will likely benefit from moving them to a cooler, more consistent area, you might consider rotating them a little bit more than usual. That way, you can give all parts of the plant equal exposure to that better light, even if it's just a few hours a day!
I guess I'll give it a try. It's just frustrating because I don't want to overdo it, but I also don't want to risk them getting too hot. Do you think I should check them more often during the day?

request.system: You are a helpful AI assistant in an ordinary conversation. Respond naturally to the participant's message.

result.content: That's a common concern—you want to keep them comfortable without stressing them out. Instead of just moving them, perhaps you could check the temperature readings in the different areas of the house periodically throughout the day. If one area is getting too warm and another is too cool, you can move them to the area that is more climate-controlled. Since you're concerned about the temperature variation, maybe check a few times a day to see which area is more stable for them.
